messages.content: Write a contemporary American fiction scene about two adult best friends walking home after a normal day. Let the conversation move naturally between the present, a memory from years ago, plans for next month, and something trivial they notice on the walk. The jumps should feel spontaneous, not like a checklist. Output only story prose.

“Did you ever call your sister back?” Lena asked.

“Not yet.” Marcus stepped around a puddle. “She wanted me to help her move that bookshelf.”

“The giant one?”

“Yeah.”

“You're going to throw your back out.”

“I’m thirty.”

“So was Dad when he started saying that.”

Marcus laughed. “That’s not encouraging.”

They passed the park, and Lena glanced toward the empty basketball court.

“Remember when you broke your wrist there?”

“I was twelve.”

“You tried to dunk.”

“I barely touched the rim.”

“You also blamed the hoop.”

“It was lower than it looked.”

“That sentence makes no sense.”

“Neither did gravity.”

Lena laughed and looked ahead. “Anyway, we're still doing the cabin trip next month, right?”

“I think so.”

“You said that last week.”

“I need to check my schedule.”

“You're the one who picked the dates.”

“I know.”

A dog barked behind a fence as they turned the corner.

Lena pointed. “That dog looks exactly like the one from the hardware store.”

Marcus looked. “You mean the dog that stole your glove?”

“My glove was hanging out of my pocket.”

“It was an easy target.”

“Exactly. Victim blaming.”

They walked another block before Marcus said, “I'll check the cabin tonight.”

“Good.”

“And I'll call my sister.”

“Also good.”

“Then you can stop reminding me.”

“I make no promises.”
